description: Liam decided 2026-11-04 (napoleon D59, replacing D34's no fixed cap) that at most 4 background Claude sessions or subagents run at once on his PC, not counting the orchestrating session and his own interactive sessions; a PC job counts as one; finished sessions are stopped. About 20 sessions (350-850 MB each) plus WSL/Docker had left 4.6 GB of 31 GB free and Claude Code killed napoleon J64's gate run for low memory. Add a [jobs] max_sessions key (default unset = no cap, so a game opts in; napoleon sets 4 at its next pin bump): `wsc jobs view --serve` buttons and `--auto` refuse a launch while the live count (claude agents --json, states working or blocked, the same read the one-session-per-name check already makes) is at the cap, naming the live sessions; `jobs next` prints the count and the cap and says to wait when it is full; a new `wsc jobs sessions [--stop-finished]` lists live and finished background sessions and, with the flag, stops the finished ones (state done) by id, never a working or blocked one and never an interactive one. Also: while a game's acceptance run holds the PC lock (its lock purpose), --auto starts nothing that needs a new window (B-line: J64 run 20261104_j64pc4 lost a pass to a window on the virtual display). Host tests with a stubbed `claude agents --json`; CONSUMING.md one line.
title: Session cap: [jobs] max_sessions, jobs sessions --stop-finished
